claims.statement: buildGraph builds a graph of Paper, Author, Venue, Keyword, Choice and Answer nodes joined by authoredBy, publishedIn, hasKeyword, cites and hasAnswer edges; graphSource/graphTrees use consolidated answers when present, else one reviewer seat.

Force layout runs in graphLayout.worker.ts: layoutHost ticks a d3-force simulation within a 12 ms budget per slice and posts Float32Array frames; layoutSettings lowers ticks and raises theta for big graphs.
graphCanvas.ts draws the graph on a 2D canvas with viewport culling, zoom-gated labels and per-edge-type dash patterns.
The node list is a folded side drawer with a toggle button showing the node count, so the canvas keeps full width while it is closed.
parseQuery reads free text, type/field/value terms, negation and depth:N (capped at MAX_DEPTH 3); selectSubgraph expands matches by that many hops.

A query starting with match runs in a small Cypher-subset engine that refuses write and advanced clauses and enforces hard limits: MAX_INPUT 4000, MAX_NESTING 32, MAX_HOPS 3, MAX_ROWS 10000 and MAX_WORK 2000000.
GraphView runs Cypher queries in graphCypher.worker.ts and terminates the worker with a timeout error after CYPHER_TIMEOUT_MS (20 s).

ExportGraphDialog exports the graph as JSON-LD, Turtle, GraphML or CSV (nodes and edges files), and the escaping helpers (turtleString, xmlText, csvCell) keep text from breaking the format, with csvCell neutralising formula-leading cells.
